cases.input: Counterparty C participates in Projects A and B with different interests and expectations.
cases.expect: One party identity resolves to two context-specific stakeholder relations with separate assertions.

cases.input: Project A reassesses influence after new evidence while Project B is unchanged.
cases.expect: A successor assessment preserves the former method, basis and result and does not affect B.

cases.input: C declares two apparently contradictory interests within one perimeter.
cases.expect: Both attributed claims remain visible pending authorized interpretation.

cases.input: A representative mandate is challenged by an affected party.
cases.expect: The mandate remains scoped and contestable and dissent stays attributable.

cases.input: Low influence is written as a permanent attribute of counterparty C.
cases.expect: The write is rejected because influence is a dated contextual assessment.

cases.input: Project A's influence rating is copied into Project B without assessment.
Stakeholder registration is treated as consent for outreach and disclosure.
cases.expect: Both actions are rejected without separate authority.
